sprint.failed_assertion: an obsolete query response cannot overwrite the latest server filter
sprint.error_verbatim: Error: The older task query was not captured within 10 seconds; recent_requests records the observed UI requests.
proven_observations: Chromium and WebKit did not complete the old-response capture prerequisite within 10 seconds; the test stopped before the intended late-response assertion could be validated in those engines.
Firefox completed all 20 checks, including the old response arriving after the newer query.
The old_response_captured flag was set only after route.fetch returned HTTP 200. The old report has no old_handler_entered field, so false cannot establish that the handler was never entered.
WebKit observed the old browser response even though old_response_captured remained false; late_fulfill_attempted was false. These facts do not establish a unique Service Worker cause.

inference_boundary.explanation: The source worker caches only the generic offline shell and CSS; it does not cache API responses. Blocking Service Workers for an interception-dependent fixture follows the official Playwright guidance, but remains a fixture correction to verify in the next run, not proof of the preceding failure's unique cause.

changes: Record the original query/filter/DOM/network prerequisites and explicit route-handler/capture progress, keeping genuine old/new requests and late-response assertions.

official_references.summary: Playwright recommends blocking Service Workers when native route interception appears to miss network events.
page.route does not intercept requests intercepted by a Service Worker; the documentation recommends serviceWorkers:'block' for request interception.
